text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. speaker: Patient
text: Physical examination shows epicanthus, upward slanting of the eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease. A grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur heard at the left mid to lower sternal border. The lungs are clear to auscultation. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The physical findings you described—epicanthus, upward slanting eyelids, low-set ears, a single transverse palmar crease, and a cardiac murmur—are classic for Down syndrome. Given your symptoms of bilious vomiting and abdominal distension, the most urgent and likely diagnosis is malrotation with midgut volvulus.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with midgut volvulus in a newborn with Down syndrome.
